Mitigated by strict non-force pushes, re-proving PR identity after every mutation, and explicit fail-closed refusal for any ancestry/identity mismatch, but the operation class (remote git mutation) keeps risk above negligible.

security_sensitive_surface_touch.rationale: Performs already-authorized git pushes to the task's own branch and GitHub PR API reads within the existing publication boundary; no new credential, auth, or permission surface is introduced beyond what finish/reconcile already had.

migration_config_release_impact.rationale: Directly changes release/publication-lifecycle behavior (how an exact open PR continues after a local CI fix, how an exact merged PR is routed) -- this is release-lifecycle-relevant even without a config schema change, distinguishing it from cases 1 and 3.

human_review_recommended.rationale: Remote branch push and PR-identity reconciliation logic sits in a class of change (shared git history / publication correctness) worth human review regardless of test coverage, since a subtle logic error could misroute a delivery even under a non-force-push guarantee.
